dialogue.text: John is expecting you in Menlo Park. It's like Macau, but with fewer casinos and more venture capital.
The ferry to the Hong Kong airport leaves from the terminal. Don't forget your passport.
{papersHere} papers already. Your postdoc is going very well, Martin.
I have a friend at SRI International in Menlo Park, John Murray. I told him about your work. He wants you.
I'll be sad to lose you, but this is a good step. Go.
How is the research going? I count {papersHere} papers from Macau so far. Three would make a very good postdoc.
Papers here tend to hide in odd places. Casinos. Markets. Guia Hill.
Welcome to UNU-IIST, Martin! The United Nations University, right here next to Guia Hill.
Here we work on rCOS: refinement of object and component systems. Models, refinement rules, proof obligations. Very rigorous.
Keep hunting for code that can never run, too. Publish three papers and come back. And try not to spend all your salary in the casinos.
Told you I'd follow you. Macau has great GUIs. The slot machines alone have thousands of buttons.
Joogie: Java into Boogie, find the code that can never run. It's going to CAV. The name stays.
I've eaten eleven egg tarts today. For science.
If you leave for America, I'm not following you there. Probably. Ask me again in a year.
Surprise! Just visiting for a week. The Mercedes couldn't make this trip, so I flew.
Error invariants got into FM! I came all the way here to tell you in person. And for the dim sum.
I fly back to Freiburg on Sunday. Brunch before the airport? Obviously.
Roulette, poker, racing, tanks. Laxino owes you and Ben a lot. Well. They paid you. So now it's even.
Gym tomorrow at seven? Then the bar at nine? The usual board meeting.
Tank Wars! Players shoot each other and the house still wins. Beautiful.
That's the whole catalog. Here's the final payment, and a thank-you from the boss.
Honestly, you and Ben built a small casino company's entire game line. Take care of yourself.
Tank Wars. Ben is on it? Good. I'll be at the bar, stress-testing the drinks.
The racing game! People bet on cars that don't exist. That's the future.
Here's your cut.
One more. Tanks. Two tanks, a maze, and a lot of explosions. Can Ben do it?
Racing game, arcade style. Talk to Ben. I'll be on the treadmill.
The poker game works, and the AI bluffs better than I do. Good job.
Your payment.
Next: something fast for the arcade floor. A racing game. Go tell Ben.
Poker next. Remember: the house always wins, but it should look fair.
The roulette works! The ball even looks like it's rolling. Laxino is happy.
Your payment, as promised.
Now we need a poker game. Ben does the pretty part, you make it correct?
Roulette. Talk to your friend Ben. I'll wait here. Bench day.
(Between two sets on the bench press, a man in a very good suit introduces himself.)
Paul. I work for Laxino. We make casino games. I hear you and your friend Ben write software.
We need house games. Start with a roulette. Interested?
Great. Let's meet at the bar when it's done. Ben does the graphics?
Science doesn't pay for the egg tarts. Think about it.
Four games shipped. Saarbrücken stairs, Macau casinos, all from my kitchen in Moscow. What's next, a spaceship?
Tell Paul I'm available for sequels.
Tank Wars! Two tanks, one maze. I'll do the explosions, you do the collision detection.
...Done. The tanks can't drive through walls anymore. Mostly.
A racing game? I've always wanted to render a car. It's basically a staircase with wheels.
...Done. Tell Paul the cars go fast. Don't tell him they're all the same car in different colors.
Poker. OK. I'll draw the cards, you write the logic that knows who won.
...Done. It took three nights and a lot of Skype. Send it to Paul.
Paul from the gym wants a roulette game? I'm in. I'll render the wheel, you make sure the math is right.
...Done. The ball lands on 17 slightly too often. Just kidding. Probably. Show it to Paul.
We sent it. Let's see what Paul says.
(Skype rings.) Martin! How's Macau? It's snowing in Moscow. It's always snowing in Moscow.
Remember Valentin's stairs? I still dream in 3D. If you find another gig over there, call me.
